identity.real_world_identity_notes: Racing truck in AMS2's Copa Truck field. Vulkan is not among the manufacturers the championship lists, so it is treated as Reiza's own entry rather than assigned a real marque, and no real-world chassis identity is claimed.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The gearbox is a five-speed plus a launch gear, and first is locked out: it cannot be selected to pull away, so the driver starts in second and races on the remaining five. A tester found first unavailable in normal running and thought it a fault, which is the lockout rather than a modelling error, and the six observed gears are that 5+1.

Article 15 of the series technical regulations mandates a lever and a mechanically operated H-pattern manual change, and in the same article leaves the gearbox itself free for all makes. The gate is therefore established by regulation, and the engagement type is left open by the series rather than merely unresearched, so the downshift blip stays unknown rather than being inferred from racing practice.

Vulkan does not appear in the championship's list of competing manufacturers, so no real-world truck is identified. Its controls are recorded from the drive and the class regulations that all Copa Truck entries share.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.vulkan-truck.20260814t195408740z-abe0c4aa by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the championship and its mandated gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The series technical regulations fix the gate - a lever, a manual H-pattern change and a mechanical linkage - and in the same article leave the gearbox free for all makes, which is why the gear count and actuation stand while the construction does not. The drive found the same gate.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim. The clutch for a shift already under way follows from gearbox construction, not from the drive.

driver_summary: Copa Truck regulations mandate a mechanically operated H-pattern manual: five racing gears plus a launch gear, and first is locked out, so pull away in second. Vulkan is not a championship manufacturer, so this is Reiza's own entry. Blip on downshifts to be safe.

deviations.basis: Gearbox construction is not established for this car, so the running-shift clutch stays unknown rather than inheriting the archetype's synchromesh technique.

Whether the driver must blip on downshifts is not established. A guided drive settles what the simulator requires; where the real car differs, that difference is recorded as an override rather than changing this value.

The gearbox type is not established, and the series is the reason. Article 15 of the Copa Truck technical regulations leaves the gearbox free for all makes, so trucks in the same field may carry different construction and there is no single value to curate. This is a settled answer rather than an outstanding one: no further reading of the regulations will close it.
